grammar: How are you? • am / is / are • I'm / he's / we're

lines: Hello, Nasser. How are you today?
I'm fine, thank you. And you?

items.focus: How are you? • OK / very well • trap: the other speaker's answer
lines: Hello, Rakan. I'm OK, thanks. And you?

items.focus: I'm / he's • who says fine? • names that are mentioned but wrong
lines: I'm OK, thanks. And you, Omar?
I'm fine, thank you. And Ali is very well today.

items.focus: we're = we are • the answer changes in the dialogue
lines: Hamad and Waleed, how are you today?
No, Hamad! We're fine. It's a lovely day.
Hello, Nasser! This is Saleh. He's my partner.
Fine, thanks. Ali is my partner, and Majed is my classmate.

items.focus: How is he? • the speaker corrects himself
lines: Omar, how are you today? Are you OK?
He's fine. No, sorry. He's very well today.

sentences.text: He says, 'Hello, class! How {are} you today?'
I say, 'Hello, Majed. How are you?'

p3.title: Hello, everyone!
p3.focus: Listening for detail: How are you? fine / very well / OK, I'm / he's / we're, partner
lines: Hello, everyone! How are you today?
We're fine, thank you, Mr Hamid. And you?
I'm very well, thanks. It's a lovely day today.
OK. Sit down with your partner, please.
Yes. My partner is Yasser. Hello, Yasser! How are you?
Hello, Saleh! I'm fine, thanks. And you?
I'm OK. And how is Rakan?
items: "I'm very well, thanks. It's a lovely day today."
Saleh says "I'm OK, thanks." Yasser is fine.

teacherNotes: Written for the English Path app (not part of the IATC weekly pack). Same format as the A1 Listening practice papers.
All names are made up. The language stays inside Week 1 Lessons 1-2: How are you?, fine, very well, OK, thanks, lovely, today, day, am / is / are, I'm / he's / we're.
Exam Skills tricks built in: the other speaker's answer (Q1), mentioned-but-wrong names (Q2), the answer changes during the dialogue (Q3), the speaker corrects himself (Q5).
